correctness.rationale: Anchor at a sampled label and rotate to zero; the other n−1 uniform positions yield the uniform (n−1)-simplex gap law. Each geodesic edge has an arc of length ≤r, whose intervening successive gaps are also ≤r. Thus short consecutive gaps generate exactly the graph's connectivity and a proper k-run has two distinct long borders. Each k-component has one such start. Translating those two gaps and applying inclusion–exclusion to the internal caps gives the stated normalized volume, and strictly feasible positive gaps exist for 0<r<1/2. The affine constraints give the required Minkowski inclusion, so Brunn–Minkowski applies in the correct relative dimension n−1. Both endpoint values vanish. On each breakpoint-free interval, a constant polynomial would force its nonzero coefficients into a Vandermonde kernel via derivative orders 1 through J+1≤k≤n−1. This excludes a plateau of maxima. For fixed k the spacing sum converges uniformly on compact c-intervals to f_k(c); the joint density of the k−1 internal gaps is bounded by n^{k−1} and a single bordering-gap probability is at most exp(−c/2). The resulting bounds c^{k−1} and exp(−c/2) confine maximizers to a compact interval, and the log derivative of f_k has one zero at log((k+1)/2). As a small boundary check, n=3,k=2 gives 2r−5r² up to 1/3 and (1−2r)² thereafter, with peak r=1/5. The frozen grid and simulations were inspected but not executed and are not needed for the analytic conclusions.

evidence: Huillet's accessible abstract concerns the joint physical lengths of equal-arc components. Decreusefond–Ferraz give the Poisson total-cluster law in Theorem 14, and Penrose–Yang study Euclidean asymptotics for the number of k-components.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For a proper component of clockwise equal arcs, the gaps of length >r cut the same runs as for the undirected geodesic graph. This makes arc-based spacing laws genuine coverage of the raw event. Total counts discard vertex-size information and Euclidean asymptotics do not give the finite-circle shape. Huillet's specific full-text coverage of such a shape was not established.

The no-plateau proof across all polynomial pieces and the bounds excluding escape on the sparse scale establish the substantive extra shape conclusions.

value.rationale: The radius that maximizes expected counts of a chosen proper size is a natural calibration of the random graph. The result controls the whole curve at finite n, excludes multiple optima despite piecewise changes of formula and gives the leading radius for every fixed k without a numerical search. That combination goes beyond recomputing spacing probabilities or invoking concavity alone.
